medSchoolStudLife.setting: Morehouse School of Medicine is situated five minutes from downtown Atlanta within the Atlanta University Center (AUC) in the historic West End. Atlanta is also home to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), over 20 major medical centers, Jimmy Carter Library & Museum, The Martin Luther King Center, and a plethora of educational, entertainment, and cultural opportunities. Atlanta's sports teams consist of the Atlanta Braves, Atlanta Falcons, Atlanta United, and the Atlanta Hawks. Home to one of the busiest airports in the world, Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, the city is a major international transportation hub. A premier city for the 21st century, Atlanta is a world class, modern city with a rich, passionate history, and an impressive legacy of leadership, progress, and inspiration.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Morehouse School of Medicine is pleased to provide the opportunity for our students and other professionals to live in the Entra-West End which offers quality housing at market rate along with other social amenities. Entra-West End is a new facility that is directly across from our campus and minutes from Downtown Atlanta. The apartment complex is designed to meet the needs of all adult learners and other professionals who desire to live in the West End area. The complex offers furnished and unfurnished studios, two and three-bedroom units. Entra-West End provides a thriving community of MSM students and professionals that is within close walking distance from classrooms and the library avoiding the expense related to a daily commute. Housing information will be included in the acceptance letter packet.  The first year housing policy requires students new to MSM to reside at Entra West End.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The Alliance Student Group, Student Health and Wellness Center, Counseling Services, Student Success Managers, Office of Student Learning and Educational Resources, and Office of Inclusive Learning & Accessibility Services.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The Office of Individualized Learning & Accessibility Services (OILAS) at Morehouse School of Medicine (MSM) is dedicated to removing physical, educational, and other barriers while creating a supportive environment for learners. OILAS operates under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) to level the playing field for students with disabilities. If MSM learners encounter academic, physical, technological, or other barriers on campus, the Access Team will collaborate with them to find creative solutions and reasonable accommodations both inside and outside the classroom. Whether learners need assistance with academic or clinical adjustments, or other services, the team is available to help students succeed while in medical school. OILAS’ goal is to create an environment where all learners and trainees have the opportunity to thrive and participate fully in the educational experience at MSM.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The Student Health and Wellness Center at Morehouse School of Medicine takes a holistic approach to health and wellness.  Our Wellness Services aim to help students integrate the physical, mental and spiritual aspects of health and well-being into their lives. Programs are held throughout the year in partnership with student organizations, campus leaders and community partners.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: MSM offers a family environment with the hallmarks of collaboration and compassion at its core.  MSM provides a nurturing and student-centered environment for individuals who are passionate about engaging the community in improving their health and well-being.  MSM is an interprofessional community of service-oriented scholars aspiring to change lives through education, research, service, and patient care.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: For the basic science years: casual attire except for days attending clinical preceptorships. Clinical years: professional attire is required with white coat.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: We have an Office of Student Learning and Educational Resources which oversees our tutorial services and in-course enrichment programs.  Faculty offer office hours for additional support.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: MS1 Students observe patient care during clinical preceptorships. Exposure to patient care continues in the second year with the Introduction to Clinical Medicine. MS3 and MS4 are the clinical years.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lectures, small groups, case and problem-based, and self-directed learning formats.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations begin in July of 3rd year. There are 6 core clerkships in the 3rd year.  4th year begins in mid June and is  comprised of 1 four-week long senior selective and 6 four-week electives
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: MSM is in the process of developing a pre-matriculation program.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance is mandatory for most lectures. Attendance is also required for small-group and problem-based learning.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The first two years of the curriculum emphasize an understanding of the principles, concepts, and a major factual background of the basic medical sciences. Exposure to clinical medicine begins in the first year through assignment to a physician preceptor and increases in the second year with introduction to clinical medicine and use of standardized patients in the clinical skills lab. Clinical education is continued through core clerkships during the third and fourth years, with 24 weeks of electives in the senior year. Student performance is evaluated primarily by letter grades. Learning resources and other support services are available to all students throughout their four years.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Morehouse School of Medicine (MSM), located in Atlanta, Ga., was founded in 1975 as the Medical Education Program at Morehouse College. In 1981, MSM became an independently chartered institution. MSM is among the nation’s leading educators of primary care physicians and was recently recognized as the top institution among U.S. medical schools for our social mission. Our faculty and alumni are noted in their fields for excellence in teaching, research and public policy.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Some research opportunities are available to enrolled students through our Office of Sponsored Programs and Research.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Community service is a core requirement of the year-long first year course, Community Health.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Research is encouraged and opportunities are provided to students.  Most students participate in research opportunities during the summer following their first year in the MD program.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Grady Health System(HS), Atlanta VA Medical Center(MC), Children's Healthcare of Atlanta, Gwinnett MC, Ridgeview Hospital, GA Regional Hospital, Columbus MC, Phoebe Putney HS, and CommonSpirit Health.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: MSM utilizes the letter based grading system for the first three years. Senior year has one letter-based clerkship (senior selective). All other 6 senior electives are Pass/Fail.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Established in 1975 as the School of Medicine at Morehouse College, Morehouse School of Medicine became independent from its founding institution in 1981.  MSM is a member of the Atlanta University Center Consortium Inc.- a consortium of five Historically Black Colleges and Universities. Through our affiliations with several medical facilities, including Grady Health System, Atlanta VA Medical Center, Children's Healthcare of Atlanta, and Ridgeview Institute for Behavioral Medicine, our students and residents are exposed to a broad patient population and have the opportunity for the best training experience possible.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Morehouse School of Medicine is dedicated to improving the health and well-being of individuals and communities; increasing the diversity of the health professional and scientific workforce; and addressing primary health-care needs through programs in education, research, and service, with emphasis on people of color and the underserved urban and rural populations in Georgia and the nation.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: 14 days if acceptance is offered before April 30, 2027. Accepted applicants in May 2027 will have 5 business days to respond. Applicants accepted in June 2027 will have 24 hours to respond.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: We require 1 composite letter of recommendation from Pre-Health Advisors or 3 letters from individual letter writers two (2) of whom must be science professors. Additionally, each letter must be on official letterhead, have the writer's name, position, organization's name, and be signed by the writer. Letters that do not meet these requirements will not be accepted.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: At least two of the letters of recommendation must come from science teachers who have taught the applicant.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: The interview day starts at 9:45 AM ET and ends at approximately 5:00 PM. Applicants are instructed to arrive to campus no later than 9:30 AM on the day of interview for check-in.  On campus parking is free for interviewees. The day's itinerary includes two faculty interviews, an overview of our curriculum, dialogue with our student ambassadors, a tour of the main campus, and a tour of our teaching hospital (Grady Hospital).  Lunch is provided.  At this time, travel stipends/reimbursements are not available.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: In person at our main campus in Atlanta, Georgia.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: Available only for applicants who permanently reside in our More in Common Alliance regions. https://www.moreincommonalliance.org/our-work/clinical-training-sites/regional-training-site-progress
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Not available as of the 2025 application cycle.  All interviews will be conducted in person.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: All eligible applicants after preliminary screening.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: MSM accepts out of state applicants. Canadian and international applicants must hold United States citizenship or permanent residency (green card) status to be considered.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Must be a United States citizen or hold permanent residency status
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Must be a United States citizen or hold permanent residency status

medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Morehouse School of Medicine conducts a holistic review of applications, taking into consideration an applicant's overall body of coursework, including community college coursework, GPA, extra curricular activities, and performance on the MCAT.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: MSM accepts letters of intent and notices of significant updates from interviewees only.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
A candidate for the M.D. degree must have aptitude, abilities, and skills in five areas:
observation, communication, motor, conceptual and integrative and quantitative, and behavior
and social. Technological compensation can be made for some handicaps in certain of these
areas, but a candidate must be able to perform in a reasonably independent manner. Students
must have the intellectual, physical, and emotional capabilities necessary to undertake the
required curriculum in a reasonably independent manner and that students must be able to
achieve levels of competence required by faculty.

medSchoolPrograms.info: The Master of Science in the Medical Sciences gives preferential treatment to in-state applicants and applicants who demonstrate socio-economic disadvantaged status and/or come from medically underserved communities with a focus on applicants who are underrepresented in medicine.

Admission into any of our dual degree programs is contingent upon acceptance into our MD program. Once accepted into the MD program, an applicant may then complete their application process for the other degree program.

medSchoolPrograms.name: Morehouse School of Medicine
medSchoolPrograms.programLength: approximately 5-6 years for the combined MD/MPH program
medSchoolPrograms.deadline: Interested students should apply after acceptance to our MD program.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Accepted applicants must select Plan to Enroll at Morehouse School of Medicine by April 30, 2026.

Accepted applicants must pay a $100 deposit (refundable if withdrawn by April 30, 2026) as directed in their acceptance letter; log into their AMCAS account and click on the (1) "Plan to Enroll" tab beginning February 15, 2026 and select Morehouse School of Medicine, (2) "Commit to enroll" tab and select Morehouse School of Medicine beginning April 30, 2026 and no later than June 8, 2026.

medSchoolAssessments.assessmentAdditionalInformation: Morehouse School of Medicine is strongly encourages all applicants to take the AAMC PREview exam. We will consider PREview scores as part of our admissions selection process.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: We offer rolling admissions. Applicants who are not offered an acceptance and are not rejected are placed on the alternate list. Alternate list applicants are frequently accepted into the class.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
The following courses must be included in undergraduate study:

Biology w/laboratory (one year) 
General Chemistry w/laboratory (one year) 
Organic Chemistry w/laboratory (one year) 
Physics w/laboratory (one year) 
College-level Mathematics (one year) 
English, including composition (one year) 

Note: An applicant may substitute one semester of Organic Chemistry w/laboratory with one semester of Biochemistry. MSM will only accept pass/fail and/or online prerequisite coursework that was completed between January 2020 to June 2024.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: It is to the applicant's advantage to demonstrate recent classroom experience as those who have been away from formal schooling may lose some foundational knowledge and may not be optimally prepared
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Selection of students for admission is made after careful consideration of many factors. These include MCAT scores, academic record, balance and depth of academic program, difficulty of courses taken, and other indicators of maturation of learning ability. Additional factors considered are extracurricular activities, hobbies, the need to work, research projects and experiences, evidence of activities that indicate concurrence with the school's mission, and evidence of pursuing interests and talents in depth.  Finally, the committee looks for evidence of those traits of personality and character essential to succeed in medicine: compassion, integrity, motivation, and perseverance. Applicant information is considered without assigning priority to any single factor. Students are admitted on the basis of individual qualifications without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, veteran status or disability.  Preferential consideration is given to applicants from Georgia.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: While there is no absolute requirement of the amount of shadowing hours, it is an expectation that medical experiences provide an understanding of healthcare delivery.
